caption: Abdur'Rahman v. Bell; No. 01-9094; October Term 2002.
Event:
Abdur'Rahman v. Bell, No. 01-9094. Merits decision, December 10, 2002. Argued November 6, 2002. On writ of certiorari to the Sixth Circuit. The granted questions concern categorical treatment of Rule 60(b) motions as successive applications and consideration of an intervening legal development affecting an earlier procedural barrier. The additional jurisdictional questions concern review of the November 27, 2001 transfer and the February 11, 2002 appellate orders.

The original petition was filed April 23, 1996. The district court transferred the entire motion as successive on November 27 and declined a certificate for lack of jurisdiction on December 4. The circuit denied a certificate on January 18, 2002. Its February 11 order separately refused rehearing/remand in original appellate Nos. 98-6568/6569 and directed the mandate; dismissed the transfer appeal, No. 01-6504, as nonappealable; and denied authorization, No. 01-6487. caption: Borden Ranch Partnership v. Army Corps of Engineers; No. 01-1243; October Term 2002.
Event:
Borden Ranch Partnership v. Army Corps of Engineers, No. 01-1243. Merits decision, December 16, 2002. Argued December 10, 2002. On writ of certiorari to the Ninth Circuit, which sustained unpermitted-discharge liability in drainages and swales, reversed the vernal-pool component and remanded for penalty recalculation. The granted questions concern deep-ripping discharges, normal farming and statutory recapture, and separate violations within one day. Jurisdiction over the remaining waters is conceded.

The approximately 8,400-acre grazing ranch was being converted toward vineyards and orchards. Ripping shanks reached roughly five to seven feet, and the trial findings describe active horizontal and vertical movement of earth, rock, sand and biological material, with filling or mounding of former channels. The trial attributed a discharge to each counted fully engaged pass: 348 passes in drainages, averaging twelve at each of twenty-nine locations, plus ten in the later-excluded pool. It imposed $1.5 million, alternatively $500,000 with restoration of four acres. The pool reversal requires a new calculation; no replacement amount has been set.

caption: A Woman's Choice–East Side Women's Clinic v. Newman; review of 305 F.3d 684; Seventh Circuit No. 01-2107
Event:
A Woman's Choice–East Side Women's Clinic v. Newman. Plenary merits decision, March 24, 2003. On review of the United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit, 305 F.3d 684, No. 01-2107, reversing the permanent injunction reported at 132 F. Supp. 2d 1150. The questions concern Indiana’s compulsory in-person communication of advance abortion information, review of trial and comparative evidence before enforcement, and preservation of separable informed-consent duties.

As construed by Indiana’s Supreme Court, it applies when the attending physician, exercising good-faith clinical judgment concerning the patient’s life and physical and mental health, finds pregnancy complications that make prompt therapeutic abortion medically necessary to address a significant threat. Severe but temporary conditions for which abortion is not medically necessary are excluded. The challenged added encounter burdens patients who remain subject to attendance after that exception operates.

caption: Center for Reproductive Law and Policy v. Bush; Second Circuit No. 01-6168; 304 F.3d 183
Event: Center for Reproductive Law and Policy v. Bush, Second Circuit No. 01-6168. Submitted on the full merits record and decided June 16, 2003. On review of the September 13, 2002 judgment affirming dismissal of domestic advocates' challenge to the 2001 restoration of the foreign-assistance Standard Clause. The district court dismissed July 31, 2001 for lack of standing. The circuit bypassed speech standing under its earlier merits precedent, recognized competitive standing but rejected equal protection, dismissed a separate notice theory and treated customary international law as duplicative while reserving independent viability. The questions concern jurisdiction, domestic communication and collaboration, and the lawful scope of the challenged condition. The plaintiffs seek declaratory and prospective relief against responsible implementing officials, including the USAID Administrator. Existing projects and lost information, audiences, distribution, witnesses and advocacy are pleaded allegations.

caption: Georgia v. Ashcroft, No. 02-182; October Term 2002.
Event: Georgia v. Ashcroft, No. 02-182. Argued April 29, 2003; decided June 26, 2003. On direct appeal from the three-judge District Court for the District of Columbia. Its April 5, 2002 judgment, 195 F. Supp. 2d 25, denied preclearance to Georgia's original 2001 Senate plan while clearing the House and congressional plans. On June 3, 2002, it cleared a revised Senate plan, 204 F. Supp. 2d 4. Georgia continues to seek authority to use the original plan. caption: Old Person v. Brown; Ninth Circuit No. 02-35171; October Term 2002.
Event: Old Person v. Brown. Merits decision, June 26, 2003. On writ of certiorari to the Ninth Circuit, No. 02-35171; certiorari granted January 17, 2003. The court of appeals affirmed on December 4, 2002, 312 F.3d 1036. The questions are whether corrected §2 totality analysis supports that judgment despite the district court's mistaken proportionality calculation, and whether impending redistricting can defeat otherwise established liability. The first appeal established the Gingles prerequisites and left rejection of intentional discrimination intact.
